author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Manage heat, throttling, battery, storage speed, and long-session stability
summary: Measure sustained rather than launch performance, control brightness and charging heat, detect thermal throttling, validate storage behaviour, and build a conservative profile for long PS2 sessions.
heroAlt: Thermal camera view of a smartphone showing warmer and cooler areas on its rear surface

blocks.text: Peak speed is not the device's playable speed

Phones boost CPU and GPU clocks when cool, then reduce them as skin, battery and silicon temperatures rise. Charging, high brightness, a thick case, warm ambient air and background recording all consume the same thermal budget as emulation. Storage can add another delayed failure when an SD card stalls, a shader/texture cache grows or free space becomes critically low.
Judge a profile only after at least twenty minutes. Do not cool a hot phone abruptly, block vents, charge under bedding or use unsafe external cooling that can create condensation.

Start with a cool device, Safe profile and a demanding repeatable route. Record room temperature, case, brightness, charge state and whether the phone is plugged in. Ensure internal storage has generous free space and removable media reports healthy before the run.

items: Cool device at a known starting charge.
Fixed brightness and network/background workload.
At least 15–20% storage free where practical.
Stable game image location and backed-up saves.
A 20–30 minute repeatable gameplay route.
1. Run the route unplugged at Safe settings and note speed/frame pacing at 5, 15 and 25 minutes.
2. If performance decays, lower internal resolution or the single dominant GPU setting one step and repeat from a cool start.
3. Compare with the protective case removed in a safe dry environment; keep brightness fixed so only heat dissipation changes.
4. Test charging separately. If charging adds heat or oscillation, play on battery and charge between sessions rather than forcing simultaneous peak loads.
5. Move a stuttering image from questionable removable storage to healthy internal storage and repeat before changing CPU or renderer settings.

blocks.text: A stable profile keeps frame pacing, audio and input consistent through the final interval, produces no Android thermal warning and leaves enough battery for a controlled exit/save. Temperature alone varies by sensor; the meaningful sign is performance decay correlated with warming under otherwise identical conditions.

items: Final ten minutes remain close to the first ten.
No charging-induced oscillation or thermal warning.
Memory-card save completes before shutdown.
Storage move changes only I/O-related stalls.
Device can cool naturally between runs.

blocks.text: When throttling appears, save in-game, exit normally and let the device cool at room temperature. Restore the last sustained profile before retesting. If storage reports errors, stop writing, back up readable saves and replace the medium; do not benchmark a failing card repeatedly.

items: Return to the last cool-run profile.
Stop charging during the session.
Remove recording/overlay workloads not needed for play.
Move verified images and saves off failing removable storage.
Fast first five minutes, slow final ten: profile exceeds sustained thermal budget.
Stutter only while charging: battery/charger heat competes with SoC cooling.
Hitches at every area load: storage path may be the limit.
Crash near full storage: caches and state writes lack working space.

blocks.text: Design the long-session profile around the weakest normal condition, not the best cold launch. A small reserve in GPU load, storage space and battery makes save writes and heavy scenes predictable. Sustainable settings usually feel smoother than a higher preset that repeatedly boosts and throttles.
